paras.text: Many of the acids present in vegetables are also present in fruits. Vegetables include citric acid, oxalic acid and benzoic acid. Oxalic acid is a naturally occurring acid found in a wide range of vegetables. ذائقے کے علاوہ پھلوں کے ایسڈز بیکٹیریائی خرابی کے آغاز کو کم کرنے کی صلاحیت کی وجہ سے محافظ کے طور پر بھی استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ زیادہ تیزابیت بیکٹیریا کو مارنے میں مدد دیتی ہے تاکہ خوراک جلدی خراب نہ ہو، مثلاً بینزوئک ایسڈ اور سوڈیم بینزوئیٹ پھپھوندی کی افزائش پر روک لگاتے ہیں؛ جو خوراک کی خرابی کی بڑی وجہ ہے۔

Self-assessment

Write the common and IUPAC names of derivatives of carboxylic acids, which yield acetic acid upon hydrolysis.

Society, Technology And Science

Some of the most common organic acids in food are found within fruits. Many people are already aware that citric acid occurs in citrus fruits such as oranges, lemons and limes, but there are lesser known acids in fruits that you may not have heard of. These include malic acid, which is found in apples and tartaric acid found in grapes. These acids provide these fruits with that distinctive sharp taste. The mixture of acid and sugar is what gives fruits their unique flavor, so foods will often be deliberately fermented in particular acids to retain or increase the flavor.

In addition to taste, acids in fruits are also used as preservatives due to their ability to reduce the onset of bacterial degradation. High acidity helps to kill bacteria so food doesn't spoil as quickly e.g. Benzoic acid and sodium benzoate have inhibitory effect on growth of fungi; major cause of food spoilage.

Many of the acids present in vegetables are also present in fruits. The key difference is that vegetables do not tend to be as acidic in their makeup, making them a potentially safer source of key acids if you struggle with acid reflux or high stomach acidity. Vegetables include citric acid, oxalic acid and benzoic acid. Oxalic acid is a naturally occurring acid found in a wide range of vegetables. Oxalates are known for binding to almost any mineral in the body. Oxalates build up insoluble compounds when binds with calcium, that can lead to kidney stones if precautions aren't taken. The principal acids found in dairy products are benzoic acid, lactic acid and a variety of fatty acids which contribute to dairy products.
